text:
Maria G: heads up — ap-southeast saw steady queue growth for the last ~20m. steady-state CPU/GPU looks fine but admission is piling up. thinking we should switch to a windowed, regional-weighted token accounting instead of the global leaky-bucket we have now

Aj Patel: can you sketch the idea? curious how it folds into existing TPM/RPM math

Maria G: short: compute an effective regional TPM from pool capacities + short-term backlog EWMA and use that as the admission ceiling per-region. this preserves global quota but prevents a starving region from sending infinite requests to a handful of healthy GPUs

Kevin L: sketch math I used in the sim:
```
pool_throughput_tok_per_sec = gpu_count * model_tok_per_sec_per_gpu * pool_efficiency_factor
region_effective_tps = sum(pool_throughput_tok_per_sec * pool_weight) - backlog_correction
region_effective_tpm = region_effective_tps * 60
backlog_correction = EWMA(backlog_tokens, alpha=0.25) / backlog_window_sec
```
example numbers: ap-south pools -> (8 * 900 * 0.9) + (2 * 400 * 0.85) = 6480 + 680 = 7160 tok/s -> ~429600 TPM before backlog correction

Vik S: that 900 tok/sec/gpu seems optimistic for 4k context runs — but fine as an example. main concern: fairness across customers if one region gets a transient bump and eats the burst credits. we should cap per-customer regional share to X% of region_effective_tpm and use a separate burst bucket with decay

Aj Patel: how does this interact with our existing token bucket refill (global) and dedicated-reserved capacity? does dedicated capacity bypass regional accounting?

Maria G: dedicated capacity stays isolated (reserved pools always have their own quotas). this is only for shared pools. global token bucket still enforces org-level quota; region_effective_tpm is an admission gate before global quota check (i.e., two-stage)

Kevin L: also add smoothing for sudden node losses: if a pool disappears, we don't zero the capacity immediately — we multiply reported pool_throughput by availability_factor = min(1, reported_healthy_gpu / total_expected_gpu) then let EWMA catch up over 30s

Vik S: propose we add two controls in the rollout:
- per-customer cap pct (default 25%)
- transient burst window (60s) with a small shared reserve (e.g., 10% of region_effective_tpm)

Maria G: agnostic to exact numbers, but +1 to both. also want the admission log to tag decisions: reason=(rate|backpressure|burst) and include capacity_estimate and backlog_ewma so ops can debug quickly

sre-bot: ALERT: ap-southeast queue latency > 800ms for 4m (was 120ms). Q length: 520 requests.

deploy-bot: scheduled config change: regional-admission-window -> enable-stage=canary on ap-southeast at 2026-03-19T21:00Z by @Maria G

Maria G: next steps: Kevin will add the backlog EWMA and availability factor to the simulator, Vik will draft rollout safety knobs (per-customer cap + burst reserve), Aj will wire the two-stage check into admission flow. I'll own canary and dashboards. planning to run 2h canary then expand if no regressions.

Aj Patel: ack, will push a PR for the admission gate wiring today.

Kevin L: PR for sim changes incoming in ~2h, I'll include the example csv sim runs and a quickplot of region_effective_tpm over a 10m spike

Vik S: will add an alert for sustained per-customer burn > cap for 3m so we can evict bad actors early

Maria G: thanks team :thumbsup:
